name: 65C02 (1983)
source: Transcribed from https://www.oxyron.de/html/opcodesc02.html (base CMOS 65C02; the 34 WDC/Rockwell-only opcodes and the 44 defined-as-NOP cells are excluded) and cross-checked against https://6502.org/tutorials/65c02opcodes.html

instructions.summary: Add memory to the accumulator with carry.
instructions.description: Adds the operand and the current carry flag to A and stores the result in A. Carry is read in before the addition and written out from the result, so chained ADCs form multi-byte addition. V is set when the signed result overflows (both inputs same sign, result the other). On the 65C02 the N and Z flags are valid in decimal mode (unlike the NMOS part, where they are undefined), and the instruction takes one extra cycle when D is set. V still has no useful meaning in BCD, which is unsigned.
examples:
CLC
ADC $10
ADC $11    ; 16-bit add, low byte then high

instructions.summary: Bitwise AND of memory into the accumulator.
instructions.description: Replaces A with A AND the operand. Used to clear selected bits with a mask. N takes bit 7 of the result and Z is set when the result is zero; C and V are untouched.

instructions.summary: Shift left one bit, into carry.
instructions.description: Shifts the operand left by one bit. Bit 7 moves into C and bit 0 becomes 0, so the operation is an unsigned multiply by two. The CMOS part optimises read-modify-write absolute,X: it costs 6 cycles rather than the NMOS flat 7, plus one when the address crosses a page.

instructions.summary: Branch if carry clear (C = 0).
instructions.description: Adds the signed 8-bit offset to the program counter when C is clear. After CMP, this means "less than" for unsigned values. No flags change.
examples:
CMP #$10
BCC lower   ; taken if A < $10

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Branch if carry set (C = 1).
instructions.description: Adds the signed 8-bit offset to the program counter when C is set. After CMP, this means "greater than or equal" for unsigned values. No flags change.
examples:
CMP #$10
BCS higher  ; taken if A >= $10

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Branch if equal (Z = 1).
instructions.description: Branches when the zero flag is set — typically after a comparison that matched, or an operation whose result was zero. No flags change.

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Test bits in memory against the accumulator.
instructions.description: Sets Z from A AND the operand, but discards the result — A is not modified. N is loaded from bit 7 of the operand and V from bit 6, independently of A. The 65C02 adds zero page,X, absolute,X and immediate modes; BIT #imm is the one exception to the rule that a mnemonic affects the same flags in every mode — it sets Z alone, leaving N and V untouched, because an immediate operand has no meaningful status bits to report.
examples: BIT $D011    ; N = bit 7, V = bit 6, Z = (A & value) == 0

instructions.summary: Branch if minus (N = 1).
instructions.description: Branches when the negative flag is set, i.e. bit 7 of the last result was 1. No flags change.

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Branch if not equal (Z = 0).
instructions.description: Branches when the zero flag is clear. The standard loop-again test after a DEX/DEY/INC. No flags change.

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Branch if plus (N = 0).
instructions.description: Branches when the negative flag is clear, i.e. bit 7 of the last result was 0. No flags change.

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Branch always.
instructions.description: Adds the signed 8-bit offset to the program counter unconditionally. Unlike JMP it is relocatable and one byte shorter, which is why position-independent CMOS code prefers it; the trade-off is the ±127-byte reach. No flags change.

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 3 (4 if taken, 5 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Force a software interrupt.
instructions.description: Pushes the program counter (already incremented past the padding byte that follows BRK) and then the status byte, sets I to mask further IRQs, and jumps through the IRQ vector at $FFFE/$FFFF. The status byte is pushed with the break bit set, which is how an interrupt handler distinguishes BRK from a hardware IRQ — that bit is not a real register flag, so it is not listed under the affected flags here.
examples:
BRK
.byte $00   ; BRK skips the following byte

instructions.summary: Branch if overflow clear (V = 0).
instructions.description: Branches when the overflow flag is clear. No flags change.

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Branch if overflow set (V = 1).
instructions.description: Branches when the overflow flag is set — after signed arithmetic, or from the external SO pin. No flags change.

modes.name: relative
modes.cycles: 2 (3 if taken, 4 if taken across a page)

instructions.summary: Clear the carry flag.
instructions.description: Sets C to 0. Required before the first ADC of an addition so no stale carry is added in.

instructions.summary: Clear the decimal flag.
instructions.description: Sets D to 0, so ADC and SBC compute in binary. D is not defined after reset, so well-behaved code clears it during startup.

instructions.summary: Clear the interrupt disable flag.
instructions.description: Sets I to 0, allowing maskable IRQs to be serviced again.

instructions.summary: Clear the overflow flag.
instructions.description: Sets V to 0. The only instruction that clears V directly; V is otherwise written by ADC, SBC, BIT, PLP and RTI, or by the SO pin.

instructions.summary: Compare memory with the accumulator.
instructions.description: Computes A minus the operand and sets the flags from the result, discarding it — A is unchanged. C is set when A is greater than or equal to the operand (unsigned), Z when they are equal, and N from bit 7 of the difference.

instructions.summary: Compare memory with the X register.
instructions.description: Computes X minus the operand and sets N, Z and C from the result without storing it. Same flag rules as CMP.

instructions.summary: Compare memory with the Y register.
instructions.description: Computes Y minus the operand and sets N, Z and C from the result without storing it. Same flag rules as CMP.

instructions.summary: Decrement a memory location by one.
instructions.description: Subtracts one from the operand and writes it back, wrapping $00 to $FF. N and Z reflect the new value; C is untouched, so DEC cannot report the borrow. The 65C02 adds accumulator mode, so DEC A decrements A directly.

instructions.summary: Decrement the X register by one.
instructions.description: Subtracts one from X, wrapping $00 to $FF, and sets N and Z from the result. The usual countdown for a loop closed by BNE.

instructions.summary: Decrement the Y register by one.
instructions.description: Subtracts one from Y, wrapping $00 to $FF, and sets N and Z from the result.

instructions.summary: Bitwise exclusive-OR of memory into the accumulator.
instructions.description: Replaces A with A XOR the operand — the standard way to flip selected bits, or to invert A entirely with EOR #$FF. N takes bit 7 of the result, Z is set when the result is zero.

instructions.summary: Increment a memory location by one.
instructions.description: Adds one to the operand and writes it back, wrapping $FF to $00. N and Z reflect the new value; C is not affected. The 65C02 adds accumulator mode, so INC A increments A directly instead of needing CLC/ADC #$01.

instructions.summary: Increment the X register by one.
instructions.description: Adds one to X, wrapping $FF to $00, and sets N and Z from the result.

instructions.summary: Increment the Y register by one.
instructions.description: Adds one to Y, wrapping $FF to $00, and sets N and Z from the result.

instructions.summary: Jump to a new address.
instructions.description: Loads the program counter with the target address. The NMOS bug where JMP ($12FF) fetched its high byte from $1200 is fixed here, at the cost of one extra cycle (indirect JMP is 6 cycles, not 5). The 65C02 also adds an absolute indexed indirect mode, JMP ($nnnn,X), which reads the target from a jump table indexed by X.

instructions.summary: Jump to a subroutine.
instructions.description: Pushes the address of the last byte of the JSR instruction onto the stack, high byte first, then loads the program counter with the target. RTS pops that address and adds one to resume. No flags change.

instructions.summary: Load a byte into the accumulator.
instructions.description: Loads the operand into A, overwriting the previous value. N is taken from bit 7 of the loaded byte and Z is set when it is zero; no other flag changes.
examples: LDA ($08,X)  ; indexed indirect: pointer at $08+X in page 0
LDA ($08),Y  ; indirect indexed: pointer at $08, then +Y

instructions.summary: Load a byte into the X index register.
instructions.description: Loads the operand into X. N takes bit 7 of the loaded byte and Z is set when it is zero. LDX is one of only two instructions with a zero-page,Y mode.

instructions.summary: Load a byte into the Y index register.
instructions.description: Loads the operand into Y. N takes bit 7 of the loaded byte and Z is set when it is zero.

instructions.summary: Shift right one bit, into carry.
instructions.description: Shifts the operand right by one bit. Bit 0 moves into C and bit 7 becomes 0, so the operation is an unsigned divide by two. N is therefore always cleared.

instructions.summary: No operation.
instructions.description: Does nothing for two cycles and affects no register or flag. $EA is the documented NOP. The CMOS part also guarantees that the 44 opcodes left unused by this variant behave as NOPs rather than as the NMOS undocumented instructions, but they are not part of the documented set and are excluded here.

instructions.summary: Bitwise OR of memory into the accumulator.
instructions.description: Replaces A with A OR the operand — the usual way to set selected bits with a mask. N takes bit 7 of the result, Z is set when the result is zero.

instructions.summary: Push the accumulator onto the stack.
instructions.description: Writes A to the stack page ($0100 + S) and decrements the stack pointer. No flags change.

instructions.summary: Push the status register onto the stack.
instructions.description: Writes the status byte to the stack and decrements the stack pointer. The break bit is pushed set, as with BRK; that bit exists only in the pushed byte, not in the register.
examples:
PHP
PLA         ; read the flags into A

instructions.summary: Push the X register onto the stack.
instructions.description: Writes X to the stack page and decrements the stack pointer. On the NMOS 6502 this needed TXA/PHA, which clobbered A. No flags change.
examples:
PHX
PHY         ; save both index registers

instructions.summary: Push the Y register onto the stack.
instructions.description: Writes Y to the stack page and decrements the stack pointer, without going through A as the NMOS part had to. No flags change.

instructions.summary: Pull the accumulator from the stack.
instructions.description: Increments the stack pointer and loads A from the stack. N and Z are set from the pulled byte.

instructions.summary: Pull the status register from the stack.
instructions.description: Increments the stack pointer and restores every real flag — N, V, D, I, Z and C — from the pulled byte. The break bit in that byte has no register to be written to.

instructions.summary: Pull the X register from the stack.
instructions.description: Increments the stack pointer and loads X from the stack. N and Z are set from the pulled byte.
examples:
PLY
PLX         ; restore in reverse order

instructions.summary: Pull the Y register from the stack.
instructions.description: Increments the stack pointer and loads Y from the stack. N and Z are set from the pulled byte.

instructions.summary: Rotate left one bit, through carry.
instructions.description: Shifts the operand left by one bit; the old carry becomes bit 0 and the old bit 7 becomes the new carry. Nine bits rotate in total, so chained ROLs shift a multi-byte value left.

instructions.summary: Rotate right one bit, through carry.
instructions.description: Shifts the operand right by one bit; the old carry becomes bit 7 and the old bit 0 becomes the new carry. Chained RORs shift a multi-byte value right.

instructions.summary: Return from an interrupt.
instructions.description: Pulls the status byte and then the program counter from the stack, restoring N, V, D, I, Z and C. Unlike RTS it does not add one to the pulled address, because the interrupt sequence pushed the address to resume at.

instructions.summary: Return from a subroutine.
instructions.description: Pulls a two-byte address from the stack and resumes at that address plus one, matching what JSR pushed. No flags change.

instructions.summary: Subtract memory from the accumulator with borrow.
instructions.description: Computes A minus the operand minus the complement of the carry flag. Carry acts as not-borrow: with C set, SBC subtracts just the operand, so SEC precedes the first SBC of a subtraction. V is set on signed overflow. On the 65C02 the N and Z flags are valid in decimal mode (unlike the NMOS part, where they are undefined), and the instruction takes one extra cycle when D is set. V still has no useful meaning in BCD, which is unsigned.

instructions.summary: Set the carry flag.
instructions.description: Sets C to 1. Required before the first SBC of a subtraction, since carry is the not-borrow input.

instructions.summary: Set the decimal flag.
instructions.description: Sets D to 1, so ADC and SBC compute in BCD. On the NMOS 6502 the N, V and Z flags are unreliable while D is set.

instructions.summary: Set the interrupt disable flag.
instructions.description: Sets I to 1, masking further IRQs. Does not mask the NMI line.

instructions.summary: Store the accumulator into memory.
instructions.description: Writes A to the addressed location. No flags change. Every indexed store costs a fixed number of cycles — the address fixup is always performed, so there is no page-crossing penalty.

instructions.summary: Store the X register into memory.
instructions.description: Writes X to the addressed location. No flags change. STX is one of only two instructions with a zero-page,Y mode.

instructions.summary: Store the Y register into memory.
instructions.description: Writes Y to the addressed location. No flags change.

instructions.summary: Store zero into memory.
instructions.description: Writes $00 to the addressed location without needing a register held at zero, so clearing memory no longer costs an LDA #$00 or disturbs A. No flags change.
examples: STZ $0400,X  ; clear a table without touching A

instructions.summary: Transfer the accumulator to X.
instructions.description: Copies A into X, leaving A unchanged, and sets N and Z from the value.

instructions.summary: Transfer the accumulator to Y.
instructions.description: Copies A into Y, leaving A unchanged, and sets N and Z from the value.

instructions.summary: Test and reset bits in memory.
instructions.description: Clears every bit of the addressed byte that is set in A, writing the result back — a read-modify-write AND with the complement of A. Z is set from the AND of A and the *original* value, so it reports whether any of the tested bits had been set. N and V are unaffected, unlike BIT.
examples:
LDA #$80
TRB $D011    ; clear bit 7, Z says whether it was set

instructions.summary: Test and set bits in memory.
instructions.description: Sets every bit of the addressed byte that is set in A, writing the result back — a read-modify-write OR with A. As with TRB, Z is set from the AND of A and the original value, so one instruction both sets a flag bit and reports its previous state.
examples:
LDA #$01
TSB $0300    ; claim a lock bit, Z says if it was free

instructions.summary: Transfer the stack pointer to X.
instructions.description: Copies the stack pointer into X and sets N and Z from the value. It moves the pointer, not stack data, so it is a register transfer rather than a stack operation.

instructions.summary: Transfer X to the accumulator.
instructions.description: Copies X into A and sets N and Z from the value.

instructions.summary: Transfer X to the stack pointer.
instructions.description: Copies X into the stack pointer. Unusually for a transfer it sets no flags, which is why startup code can do LDX #$FF / TXS without disturbing them.

instructions.summary: Transfer Y to the accumulator.
instructions.description: Copies Y into A and sets N and Z from the value.
